beats.text: This will take two days. Famous last words.
Students guessed how long their thesis would take. On average: about thirty-four days.
Even their worst-case guess was forty-nine days.
The real average: fifty-five. Only about three in ten finished on time.
It's called the planning fallacy. We picture the plan. Not the interruptions.
The fix: check how long it took last time. Not how long it should take.

sources: Buehler, Griffin & Ross (1994). Exploring the planning fallacy. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 67(3). 37 students: predicted 33.9 days, worst case 48.6, actual 55.5; about 30% finished by their prediction. Via Wikipedia 'Planning fallacy'.
